requirements.label: A qualifying upper-secondary examination

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. Endvidere skal ansøgeren have gennemført enkeltfag på gymnasialt niveau svarende til overbygning, jf. reglerne om overbygning i højere forberedelseseksamen (hf-eksamen) i lov om gymnasiale uddannelser.

requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.
requirements.note: If you pay tuition, AAU says you cannot apply in the year you earn your IB: your documentation deadline is 1 May. Non-EU applicants should check whether a residence-based fee exemption applies. The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

sources.title: DP Course Results (formerly the IB Certificate) of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three subjects at HL, are a qualifying examination in Denmark on the same terms as a two-year hf without overbygning: they give access to erhvervsakademi- and professionsbachelor programmes through quota 1 and quota 2, and to a university bachelor only after two successive raises of upper-secondary subject level, at least one to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag. Course Results under 18 points, or containing any subject at grade 1 or 2, are not a qualifying examination at all. A full IB Diploma of 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark.
sources.quote: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2. contextNotes.topic: At Aalborg you will spend every semester in a group
contextNotes.text:
Aalborg's teaching model is problem-based project work, and it is not a flavour on top of ordinary lectures — it is the structure of the degree. Every semester is built around a large written project done with a group of fellow students, alongside more conventional teaching. UNESCO has its only professorial chair in problem-based learning there, which gives some sense of how seriously the university takes it.

Worth thinking about honestly before you apply, in both directions. If you liked IB group work and Extended Essay research, this is close to an ideal fit. If your best work happens alone and you found group assignments the worst part of the Diploma, three years of this is a real consideration — not a reason to rule Aalborg out, but a reason to know what you are choosing.
